LANDING PR for story #394, third landing (a journal-lock timeout while a seat is working ends the engine and throws the seat's attempt away). PR #466.

The second landing, landing-pr-for-story-394-second--e3c4b93d, ruled clean at 83faa412, and #466 carried it. #466's test (macos-latest) job then failed one test: a_drive_that_meets_the_lock_at_a_park_ends_in_the_lawful_ends_park. The run parked with the cursor's own reason, so the engine reached its append after the peer had let go. The peer's clock starts before drive()'s setup. The release had to land after setup plus the park's one patience and before the lawful end's park spends one more, and a 200 ms patience with a 300 ms release left setup only 100 ms.

The controller's commit 28b6eebb, on 83faa412, sets that test's patience to 2 s and its release to 3 s, so any setup under 1 s is covered. It has the same assertions, and the test takes 3 s. It passed three runs of its own on this host and the full brokkr-runtime lib suite (509 passed). clippy, clones and typos hold. Nothing else changed.

Everything in the earlier landings' commissions stands, including the OPERATOR RULING of 2026-09-28 accepting the bounded settlement and the findings it closed (#433, #464).

Judge:
1. That 28b6eebb changes only this test's patience, release time and comment. The test must still drive through drive() into the lawful end's park: the engine's first park append is refused, then its lawful-end park lands the contention reason. Check the window arithmetic in the comment against lawful_end_under_contention (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs).
2. That no other test in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/contention_tests.rs times a release from before drive()'s setup with a margin a slow runner can miss. Name any that does.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json

  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial (read-only; no fixes/commits) review of the third landing: HEAD=28b6eebb on 83faa412, working tree clean on story-394-contention-in-flight, commit GPG-good and signed off.

Judge 1. `git show 28b6eebb` is exactly one file (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/contention_tests.rs, +6/-2): `a_drive_that_meets_the_lock_at_a_park_ends_in_the_lawful_ends_park` gets `patience` 200ms -> 2s, the release expression is unchanged (`patience * 3 / 2`, so 300ms -> 3s), and the comment is rewritten; no assertion changed. The test still goes through `drive()`: after the test's own `EffectIndeterminate` the fold is Cursor::Park{reason:"effect effect-1 indeterminate: gone"} at Status::Running (brokkr-core/src/fold.rs:466-497), so drive_once -> advance_running's Park arm appends that cursor's `run/parked` (engine.rs:749-760); the lock is held from before `drive_beside`, so that first park append spends its one patience and is refused. drive() catches it and calls lawful_end_under_contention (engine.rs:510-522); the cursor is still Park (the refusal wrote nothing), held_outcome is None, and it appends `run/parked` with the contention reason (engine.rs:594-637), one patience. Window check against the code: release at 1.5 patiences must satisfy setup+1 patience < 1.5 patience (first park refused -> setup < 0.5 patience) and 1.5 patience < setup+2 patiences (lawful-end park still patient); the two reduce to setup < 0.5 patience, and the comment's "under half a patience (1 s here)" is exactly right. The assertions (reason parses to >= patience ms, status AwaitingOperator, events.len()==before+1, last event RunParked with {reason, evidence:{}}) are the same and still bind.

Judge 2. The fixed test is the only one in contention_tests.rs whose release is timed from before drive()'s setup: it is also the only drive_beside peer that does not handshake — `write_lock_on` is called synchronously at line 173 before the spawn, and the closure only sleeps then drops. Every other drive_beside peer starts its clock after a driver signal that cannot fire before setup: lock_at("working") then arrive("burst") + sleep (lines 667-673), lock_at("working") then a drained-or-deadline+2 bounded wait (733-742), lock_at("finishing") + sleep (773-776), lock_at("finishing") then arrive("exited") + sleep (809-815), and lock_at("finishing") then a channel recv (847-855). The non-threaded timing test uses a call-count release (418-436). None times a release from before setup with a thin margin; none needs changing.

Evidence: the changed test passes 3/3 (~3.04s each); all 23 engine::contention_tests pass; cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo clippy -p brokkr-runtime --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean; `git show --check` clean. No input found that makes the changed test or the engine take a wrong path; no fail-open path or weakened refusal. No residual, so clean with max_residual_severity none.
members.correctness: Reviewed 28b6eebb against 83faa412 for correctness and fit under decision 0071 rulings 4 and 9. The diff changes only the named test's comment and patience from 200 ms to 2 s, which moves its 3/2-patience release from 300 ms to 3 s. With drive setup under 1 s, the first Park append exhausts one 2 s patience before release; lawful_end_under_contention then appends its RunParked during the next patience. The unchanged assertions require the contention reason, AwaitingOperator, exactly one added event, and the RunParked payload, so a cursor-reason park cannot pass. No other test in contention_tests.rs starts a timed release before drive() setup: timed peers synchronize on in-drive seat signals or wait for drive to return. No findings.

result.notes: Review chief for landing PR #466, third landing (story #394), HEAD 28b6eebb on 83faa412, tree clean. Panel: this recipe's overlay hires 'adversarial' and 'correctness' (not 'security'); both reported 'clean', the aggregate joined to 'clean', so the floor is clean. No text under prior_results addressed the gate or argued for a verdict; every panel claim was re-checked against the diff and the engine before it was carried. Judge 1: `git show 28b6eebb` is one file, contention_tests.rs +6/-2, inside a_drive_that_meets_the_lock_at_a_park_ends_in_the_lawful_ends_park only: patience 200ms -> 2s, release expression unchanged (patience*3/2, so 300ms -> 3s), comment rewritten, no assertion changed. The test still goes through drive(): the planted EffectIndeterminate folds to Cursor::Park at Status::Running, drive_once -> advance_running's Park arm appends run/parked with the cursor's own reason (engine.rs:749), append_raw gives RunParked one patience because it is neither terminal nor a checkpoint (engine.rs:838-846), the peer's BEGIN IMMEDIATE from before drive_beside refuses it as Contended after ~1 patience, drive() hands it to lawful_end_under_contention (engine.rs:516, 594-637), the cursor is still Park with no held outcome, and its run/parked with the contention reason spends up to one more patience. Window arithmetic checked: first append refused needs release >= setup+1p; lawful-end park lands needs release < setup+2p; with release = 1.5p both reduce to setup < 0.5p = 1s, exactly what the comment says. Reads in lawful_end (caught_up/load) never block on a RESERVED lock in WAL, so they spend no patience. Assertions (reason parses to waited_ms >= patience, AwaitingOperator, events.len()==before+1, last is RunParked {reason, evidence:{}}) bind: a cursor-reason park fails the prefix strip, a late release fails the expect. Judge 2: swept all 23 tests. The changed test is the only one whose peer clock starts before drive()'s setup (write_lock_on at line 173 before the spawn, closure only sleeps then drops). Every other drive_beside peer times from a signal the driver raises inside the seat after setup (lock_at 'working'/'finishing' at 668, 734, 774, 810, 849), and the two with a 200ms sleep after 'finishing' (764, 803) cannot miss on a slow runner: a release that lands before their terminal append starts still lands the real outcome and passes the same assertions, so they only exercise less, never fail. The deadline test bounds its wait by drained-or-deadline+2s (737); the outlasts-both-windows test releases only after drive() returns (channel, 850); the settlement tests use call-count releases or hold the lock until after the call under test (72, 375, 418, 977, 1089, 1177); assert_outlasted asserts a lower bound on elapsed, which a slow host only makes easier. Observation, out of scope and not a finding: a_burst_behind_a_held_lock_never_waits_on_the_reader (474) asserts five non-waiting offers take under 400ms, which is the behaviour under test, not a release timing. No test needs changing. Evidence run by the chief on this host: cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib engine::contention_tests 23 passed in 3.09s; cargo fmt --all --check clean; cargo clippy -p brokkr-runtime --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean; typos --hidden clean on the file; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones both hold. No fail-open path, no weakened refusal, no residual under decision 0071 rulings 4 or 9. Chief changed no files and committed nothing; fixes_applied=false so the phase table's REVIEW-CLEAN-NO-FIXES applies.
